speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, have you experienced any recent head trauma or been exposed to loud noises prior to this sudden onset of vertigo?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. To help distinguish between a vestibular migraine, BPPV, and Meniere's disease, how would you describe the nature of the vertigo: is it a brief spinning sensation triggered by head movements, or a continuous feeling lasting longer? Also, do you notice any hearing loss, ringing in the ears, or a sensation of fullness in your affected ear?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Sudden-onset sensation of the room spinning. I also have Nausea, Vomiting, Dizziness.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV).

Given the brief duration (3 minutes) and lack of auditory symptoms, I am requesting a Dix-Hallpike maneuver test and a bedside head impulse test to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Dix_Hallpike_Manuever; REQUEST TEST: Head_Impulse_Test.
